# Tests that cannot pass on the CI runner for host reasons, not code reasons,
# and tests that skip themselves on it.
#
# Format: two kinds of lines. An entry names a test that fails on the runner.
# It holds exactly a package import path, one space and a test path. A line
# for a test that skips itself on the runner holds the word "skips-itself",
# one space, and the same two things. A test path is a top-level test name,
# or the path that go test prints for a subtest. Empty lines and lines whose
# first character is "#" are ignored. Any other line is an error.
# .github/ci/go_test_gate.py reads this file and documents the rules.
#
# The entries come first in this file, and the lines for tests that skip
# themselves after them, under their own heading.
#
# An entry applies only to the package it names. An entry for a whole test
# stands for that test with all of its subtests. An entry for a subtest
# stands for that subtest alone. The step "Test" skips the entries and runs
# everything else. Tests run unchanged everywhere else.
#
# Every entry must still fail on the runner. The step "Listed tests still
# fail" judges every entry twice, in a run of its whole package with nothing
# skipped and in a go test of its own, and fails the run when an entry
# passes, skips itself or does not run in one of the two. So an entry cannot
# outlive its reason: a change that makes a listed test pass on the runner,
# by porting it or otherwise, has to delete its line in the same change.
#
# Only a failure that the testing package reports counts: t.Fatal, t.Error
# or a panic. A test that ends the process without reporting, for example
# with os.Exit or log.Fatal, cannot be listed, because nothing tells it from
# a test that was running when something else stopped the test binary.
#
# Name the narrowest thing that fails. Where one subtest fails and its
# siblings pass on the runner, the entry names that subtest, so the siblings
# stay in the gate. A change that adds a test which can only pass off the
# runner adds its entry here itself.
#
# Subtests that cannot be listed. For each of them, list the whole test:
#
#   - A subtest whose printed path has a part that is empty or that holds a
#     character other than an ASCII letter, a digit, "_" or "-". go test
#     prints a space as "_", and the parts are what stands between the "/".
#   - A subtest that go test numbers with "#01" because its name repeats.
#   - A subtest that has subtests of its own, or a neighbour whose name
#     starts with its name and a "/". go test reads a test path as the start
#     of a path, so the skip for TestA/x also covers every test whose path
#     starts with "TestA/x/". Both steps check this.
#
#     The step "Test" runs a package that has an entry for a subtest a
#     second time and has go test write down every test that it skips
#     there. The step fails unless those tests are exactly the entries of
#     the package. So it names a neighbour that an entry takes with it,
#     also one that the test starts only when the listed subtest did not
#     fail, and it names an entry that skipped nothing.
#
#     The step "Listed tests still fail" fails the run when the run of an
#     entry starts another test under the path of that entry. Where that
#     test is a subtest of the listed one and it is what fails, the entry
#     can name it instead.
#
# A subtest that a listed subtest x would start itself does not start while
# x is skipped. It is part of x, and nothing but x is lost with it.
#
# The way to shorten this list is to port a test so that it passes on a Linux
# runner without weakening it.

# Remote Alpha operator-host tests in the root package.

# The test process must run as the account named "ds". The second test also
# needs the macOS /private/tmp path for one subtest.
#
# The first two tests are listed whole on purpose, although some of their
# subtests pass on the runner. The TLS status bootstrap refuses a caller that
# is not "ds" at its first identity check, so a subtest that expects a
# refusal passes there without reaching the custody check it is named for.
# Keeping those subtests in the gate would claim a check that does not happen.
execution-substrate TestRemoteAlphaESServiceTLSStatusFailureWitnessBootstrapOwnedTerminal
execution-substrate TestRemoteAlphaESServiceTLSStatusRootLoadedStageCustody
execution-substrate TestRemoteAlphaESServiceTLSStatusStageFIFOSubstitution
execution-substrate TestRemoteAlphaOperatorRecoverySessionESTLSStatusStageFIFORefusal

# The test stages under the macOS /private/tmp path.
execution-substrate TestRemoteAlphaOperatorRecoverySessionESTLSStatusRemoteWrapperTrap

# The host needs an account named "ds" and the macOS /private/tmp path.
execution-substrate TestRemoteAlphaP0tGrammarDiagnosticBootstrapLifecycleComposition
execution-substrate TestRemoteAlphaP0tGrammarDiagnosticPriorReaderCloseSuppression
execution-substrate TestRemoteAlphaP0tGrammarDiagnosticV2VersionedBootstrap

# The checker reads the host's real modprobe configuration, which the fixture
# cannot replace. A host that already blocks algif_aead reports
# mitigated_not_fixed.
execution-substrate TestRemoteAlphaRuntimeSecurityBoundaryCVE31431UnprovedMitigationStaysVulnerable
execution-substrate TestRemoteAlphaRuntimeSecurityBoundaryCVE31431VulnerableWithoutMitigationBlocks

# The test assumes that /usr/bin and /bin hold no working systemctl.
execution-substrate TestRemoteAlphaRuntimeSecurityBoundaryCheckMissingToolsStayHonest

# es/app: a go command in the system directories of the harness PATH defeats
# the missing-Go fixture of this one subtest in each test. The runner image
# has such a go command. The three other subtests of each test stay in the
# gate.
execution-substrate/es/app TestSupportedLocalSetupExactGoPreflightBeforeMutation/local_build_path_rejects_missing_Go_before_mutation
execution-substrate/es/app TestSupportedLocalProofExactGoPreflightBeforeMutation/local_build_path_rejects_missing_Go_before_mutation

# es/app: the mounted-source witness binds its evidence to a source-identity
# envelope that an operator supplies from a governed source checkout, in the
# four ES_MOUNT_WITNESS_* variables. The runner has no such checkout and no
# such values, and the test fails on purpose when they are missing. Giving it
# made-up values would make its evidence false.
execution-substrate/es/app TestSubmitFlowMountsGovernedArtifactAndLifecycleWithInstalledSourceIdentity

# es/admission/internal/reliablesubmit: historical-opener probes. They need
# test binaries built from older trees with an overlay kept outside this
# repository (the ES_REPLAY_*_PROBE variables).
execution-substrate/es/admission/internal/reliablesubmit TestSQLiteV4PreviousSchema3BinaryRefusesWithoutMutation
execution-substrate/es/admission/internal/reliablesubmit TestSQLiteV3OldBinaryRefusesWithoutMutation


# Tests that skip themselves on the runner.
#
# A test that calls t.Skip takes itself out of the gate. The step "Test"
# fails the run unless the tests that skipped themselves are exactly the
# tests named below, each in the package of its line. So a test that skips
# itself on the runner needs a line here with its reason, in the change that
# adds the skip. And a line cannot outlive its reason: when the test passes
# on the runner, fails there or no longer exists, its line has to go in the
# same change. The log of the step names every test that skipped itself,
# with what the test wrote.
#
# A line stands for exactly the test or subtest it names. A subtest that
# skips itself needs a line of its own, and the name rules for subtests
# above hold for it. A line must not name an entry, lie inside one or hold
# one: what lies inside an entry does not run in the gate.
#
# These tests do not run in the step "Test". The way to shorten this part of
# the list is to give the runner what a test needs, or to port the test.
#
# The lines of the root package are different. The step "Listed root-package
# tests pass as root" runs every test that this part names for the package
# execution-substrate once more through sudo, and fails unless each passes
# there. So a test of the root package belongs here only when it skips itself
# for want of root. .github/ci/go_test_as_root.py gives the rules.

# Root package: real-kernel tests of the PID-namespace containment of the
# Remote Alpha TLS status collector. Creating a PID namespace needs root on
# Linux. Each test asks the kernel by an attempt in a child of its own and
# skips itself when the kernel refuses. These five run as root in the step
# named above.
skips-itself execution-substrate TestRemoteAlphaESServiceTLSStatusChildNamespaceRealCollectorDeath
skips-itself execution-substrate TestRemoteAlphaESServiceTLSStatusChildNamespaceRealDeafAnchor
skips-itself execution-substrate TestRemoteAlphaESServiceTLSStatusChildNamespaceRealDescendants
skips-itself execution-substrate TestRemoteAlphaESServiceTLSStatusChildNamespaceRealKernel
skips-itself execution-substrate TestRemoteAlphaESServiceTLSStatusChildNamespaceRealSiblings

# es/admission: the opt-in stress test of the directory swap race in the
# startup probe, and the attacker process it starts (finding RT-3 of the
# red-team of pull request #20). A race is not a gate: the stress test runs
# only as root and only when ES_PROBE_SWAP_STRESS_ROUNDS is set, and the
# attacker runs only in the process the stress test starts. They skip
# themselves on every host. TestExecutionRootProbeHandsNoDirectoryToAnotherUser
# gates the same rule without a race.
skips-itself execution-substrate/es/admission TestExecutionRootProbeDirectorySwapStress
skips-itself execution-substrate/es/admission TestExecutionRootProbeDirectorySwapStressAttacker

# es/admission/internal/reliablesubmit: helper processes. Another test of the
# package starts the test binary a second time with a variable set, and only
# that process runs the body. Run as a test, each of the two has nothing to
# do. They skip themselves on every host.
skips-itself execution-substrate/es/admission/internal/reliablesubmit TestPrivateReplayObjectAllocatorHelperProcess
skips-itself execution-substrate/es/admission/internal/reliablesubmit TestSQLiteClaimStoreLockHelperProcess
